src_fixes_needed: 1. Nautilus template (src/fork_linux/data/templates/fork_linux_nautilus.py.in): it asks for gi.require_version('Nautilus', '4.0') and then '3.0'. Nautilus 50 (Ubuntu 26.04) has already loaded version 4.1, so both calls raise 'Namespace Nautilus is already loaded with version 4.1' and the extension never loads, so there is no 'Open in Fork' item. Fix: try '4.1', '4.0', '3.0' in turn and keep the first that works; if none does, use the namespace already loaded. Unit test: in tests/test_desktop_integration.py, parametrize test_nautilus_extension over the loaded version (4.1, 4.0, 3.0, 4.2) with a fake gi that refuses any other version.

2. desktop_integration.py: a Nautilus that is already running never loads an extension installed after it started, and install prints nothing about it. Thunar has THUNAR_RESTART for the same case. Fix: add NAUTILUS_PROGRAMS = ('nautilus',) and a NAUTILUS_RESTART warning ('nautilus -q'). Emit it from _install_kind when the extension file actually changed, and from remove() when the extension was removed, only if a nautilus process is running. Unit tests: test_running_nautilus_is_told_to_restart and test_no_restart_notice_without_nautilus.

3. display.py: _from_gnome (scaling-factor x text-scaling-factor) runs before xrdb. With the display at 200 % and Large Text (x 1.25), Xft.dpi is 240 but fork-linux answers 125 instead of 250. A scaling-factor of 2 left in dconf makes it answer 200 on a 100 % Wayland desktop. Fix: DESKTOP_PROBES['gnome'] = _from_xrdb, because gsd-xsettings publishes Xft.dpi as display scale x text scaling. Unit tests: test_gnome_asks_xft_dpi_before_its_gsettings (250, 100, 200) and test_gnome_without_xft_dpi_falls_back_to_its_gsettings.

All three were checked on a copy of the tree: with the patches, tests/test_display.py and tests/test_desktop_integration.py gave 139 passed. GNOME facts the recipe relies on: mutter 50 has no X11 mode (--x11, --replace and --nested are gone), so the recipe runs it with --wayland --headless --virtual-monitor 1920x1080 and its own Xwayland. GDK_BACKEND=x11 is needed so xdotool can see the Nautilus and Ptyxis windows. systemd-run is diverted in the image, otherwise every Ptyxis tab shows 'Failed' because there is no systemd user manager. Nautilus 50 opens the context menu with the Menu key, not Shift+F10. xdg-utils recognises 'ubuntu:GNOME' only through gnome-session's org.gnome.SessionManager, so the recipe uses XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=GNOME. Nautilus started as a D-Bus service quits when idle, so FileManager1 is often only activatable. The root window of rootless Xwayland cannot be captured, so screenshots capture the window itself.

Framework assumption found: Xwayland drops the very first XTEST event after it starts. The Budgie recipe works around it with a warm-up 'xdotool key shift' in labwc's startup command. labwc starts Xwayland with -terminate 10, so if Xwayland idles out and restarts mid-run, the first key could be lost again (not seen in the 11/11 run).

Generic framework changes, all backwards compatible: (a) dekit.Session.start_file_manager accepts an empty file_manager_service, meaning the session starts the file manager; it then waits for FileManager1 to have an owner and takes Desktop.session_exports (a new field, default ()) from that process's environment; (b) test_scale_detection_follows_the_desktop applies a scale's settings before session.restart as well as after, because lxqt-session reads session.conf only at login; (c) the Thunar uca-WARNING log check runs only for THUNAR_UCA; (d) new URL_QTXDG_MAT handler, which registers the stub browser with 'qtxdg-mat def-web-browser --set' because xdg-mime default sets only its first MIME type on LXQt; (e) PCMANFM_QT_FMA reuses _check_fma_action. Lint: ruff, hadolint, yamllint, actionlint and no-suppressions-lint pass; test_docker, test_workflows, test_no_suppressions_lint and test_repo_hygiene pass on the committed tree (372 passed).
